source.title: MedSAE: Dissecting MedCLIP Representations with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Riccardo Renzulli; Colas Lepoutre; E. Cassano; Marco Grangetto

page_placements.theme: Additive composition in vision and diffusion embeddings

record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse autoencoders and an averaging-based probe to MedCLIP, a medical vision-language model, and reports results on its representations.
record.gate_note: The study tests SAE feature recovery and alignment in MedCLIP. It also probes whether composite-image embeddings are approximately reconstructed from component embeddings; that result does not test the specific toy-network geometry in V1. Hyperparameter-search values used to select a configuration are not recorded as results. Cited results from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: Trains a ReLU SAE on MedCLIP-ResNet image embeddings and reports whether sparse, concept-aligned features can be recovered, compared against raw neurons and a shuffled control. This is a result on V4 in a new setting: a medical vision encoder rather than an LLM.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors claim an averaging probe shows MedCLIP embeddings approximately satisfy the linear superposition hypothesis. Also add that they flag limits: dead units, sensitivity of automated naming, and a single backbone.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a ReLU SAE trained on MedCLIP image embeddings, label-correlation and entropy measures, MedGemma naming and detection, and composite-image averaging probes; it does not reproduce the original toy-network experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Interpretability measures vary across sparsity–reconstruction trade-offs; entropy increases again beyond a sparsity level described as low L0. Automated naming is described as sensitive to the selection of top-activating samples.

fits_no_version.finding: Composite-image MedCLIP embeddings are reconstructed from the two component embeddings at cosine similarity 0.97, with weights near 0.5 but std about 0.32.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MedCLIP image embeddings combine approximately linearly under spatial composition of the input images.

record.problems: Experiments use one MedCLIP-ResNet backbone and CheXpert. The authors report 30% dead neurons, say automated naming is sensitive to the selected top-activating samples, and note that human expert validation remains necessary. Several comparisons are shown only as plots without numerical values.

untested.parts: No toy networks, no sparsity-driven phase transition and no feature geometry. The composite-image linearity probe is about input averaging, not overlapping feature directions.
Does not measure whether important features get dedicated dimensions. The capacity–sparsity tension is mentioned only as speculation about dead units.
No LLMs. Only one vision encoder (MedCLIP-ResNet, last layer) on one dataset (CheXpert). Does not directly test how features spread across raw neurons.
No completeness, stability or canonicality tests. Feature alignment is assessed only for the top-scoring neurons.

missing.what: 30% dead neurons in the selected SAE

record.verdict_notes: V4 names LLMs; this study tests a CNN vision encoder, so the verdict extends V4 to a new kind of system. Table 2 rows are the top-selected neurons, so they show that well-aligned features exist, not how common they are. Detection accuracy depends on MedGemma 4B-it with 4-bit quantization as the judge.

versions.untested_parts: The composite-image probe addresses linear reconstruction in MedCLIP, but does not test small networks with more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping near-orthogonal directions, or the claimed sparsity-dependent transition and regular geometry.
Does not test whether feature importance determines dedicated dimensions versus shared capacity. Dead neurons and capacity–sparsity tension are discussed, not measured as this account predicts.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE-recovered features in MedCLIP on CheXpert, not feature spreading across neurons in LLMs or generality across other models and settings.
Tests semantic alignment and detection accuracy for some SAE features, but not whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

relationships.condition: MedCLIP-ResNet last-layer embeddings, CheXpert, selected ReLU SAE (×16 expansion)
relationships.reason: The SAE finds 21 neurons with detection accuracy above 70% versus 2 raw neurons, and has higher density at high accuracy, with a sparse code (0.20% L0) at 0.98 FVE (R2, R3, R4, R7, R10–R30).
relationships.display_finding: The SAE gave 21 units with detection accuracy above 70% against 2 raw neurons, with higher density at high accuracy and a sparse code (0.20% L0) at 0.98 fraction of variance explained.
